experiment_context.purpose: 直流快充动态过程的全量CAN Observation Discovery；不预设本次数据的Signal角色、Evidence Gap或结论
experiment_context.system_scope: 车辆侧直流快充连接、状态、高压、能量和热管理可观察边界
experiment_context.analysis_scope: 全量bus-key、DBC coverage、Known/Residual/Unknown机器观察及候选压缩

initial_conditions: no requirement to begin from sleep

planned_phases.action: connect charging interface and record recognition and locking when independently observed
perform authorization and request charging start; actual timing may vary
check whether charging actually established using independent vehicle and EVSE evidence
observe EVSE and Pack voltage current power capability state and thermal context
observe a conditional short stable interval if naturally available
request one normal stop if charging has not already ended
confirm output stopped and lock released before disconnecting
retain an optional post-disconnect observation tail

procedure_constraints: planned action order may change to follow the EVSE operating procedure
charging may start or stop earlier than the nominal planned time
a planned steady interval exists only if the observed process naturally becomes stable
Pack current alone does not confirm that EVSE output stopped
planned actions do not establish observed event times

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Distinguish nine-terminal mechanical interface conditions from confirmed physical connection.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Independent evidence is required for mechanical contact and connection confirmation.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Distinguish connection confirmation from lock request, lock execution, lock feedback, and confirmed lock.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: A single state label cannot satisfy all locking stages.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Distinguish A+ and A- contact, auxiliary supply establishment, actual controller wake, and charge-ready state.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Downstream activity alone does not prove each upstream condition.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Identify communication link, handshake or initialization, version compatibility, and parameter exchange where observable.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Generic protocol stages do not prove a fixed internal ECU sequence or unobserved protocol messages.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Identify EVSE Capability without substituting Vehicle Capability, Vehicle Request, or Actual.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Capability requires validated boundary variables or explicit insufficient evidence.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Identify Vehicle Capability without substituting EVSE Capability, Vehicle Request, or Actual.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Vehicle allowed voltage/current/power require validated vehicle-boundary evidence.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Identify Vehicle Request voltage and current independently of Capability and Actual.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Request power is derived from synchronized request voltage/current unless an independent request-power field is validated.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Identify Permission and Safety Gate separately from contactor state, high-voltage path, and energy transfer.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Actual or contactor observations cannot alone prove permission.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Identify high-voltage path request, action, feedback, voltage matching, and establishment within observable limits.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Contactor state alone does not prove energy transfer.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Distinguish EVSE Actual voltage/current/power from Pack Actual voltage/current/power at their measurement boundaries.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Cross-boundary comparison requires synchronized and semantically validated measurements.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Assess the continuous Capability, Request, EVSE Actual, and Pack Actual relationship without collapsing roles or assuming causality from proximity.
Identify thermal state, thermal demand, execution, and effects on capability or request where supported.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Thermal correlation requires validation and an alternative-condition check for causal attribution.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Identify protection monitoring, limiting action, stop request, and safe shutdown without inventing fault causes.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: Protection interpretation requires applicable safety and fault-state evidence.

semantic_evidence_questions.semantic_need: Describe controlled stop across Request, EVSE Actual, Pack Actual, high-voltage path, communication closeout, and safe unlock.
semantic_evidence_questions.sufficiency_rule: CAN state time is not human action time, and a missing initiator remains an evidence gap.

semantic_boundaries: A+ and A- mechanical contact is not proof that auxiliary low-voltage supply is established.
Auxiliary low-voltage supply establishment is not proof that the vehicle actually woke.
Capability, Request, and Actual are distinct semantic roles.
Permission, contactor state, and energy transfer are distinct states or results.
EVSE Actual and Pack Actual belong to different measurement boundaries.
A generic communication process does not prescribe one vehicle ECU implementation sequence.
DBC labels and temporal proximity do not independently confirm semantic role or causality.

control_mainlines.name: Capability, Request, Permission, and Actual control

control_tree_nodes.name: Nine-terminal physical interface
control_tree_nodes.definition: Mechanical availability of PE, CC1, CC2, DC+, DC-, A+, A-, S+, and S-; contact order is a physical-interface prior and not proof of electrical function establishment.

control_tree_nodes.name: Connection confirmation
control_tree_nodes.definition: Vehicle-side and EVSE-side connection confirmation are distinct observations and must not be inferred solely from mechanical contact.

control_tree_nodes.name: Interface locking
control_tree_nodes.definition: Lock request, lock execution, lock feedback, and confirmed locked state are distinct.

control_tree_nodes.name: Auxiliary supply and vehicle wake
control_tree_nodes.definition: A+ and A- contact, auxiliary low-voltage supply establishment, wake conditions, controller wake, and charge-ready state require separate evidence.

control_tree_nodes.name: Digital communication handshake
control_tree_nodes.definition: S+ and S- physical readiness, communication link establishment, endpoint online state, handshake, initialization, and communication validity are generic functions; implementation ownership is vehicle-specific.

control_tree_nodes.name: Version and parameter exchange
control_tree_nodes.definition: Protocol compatibility, version exchange, battery parameters, EVSE capability, vehicle capability, and preparation state are distinguishable communication-stage concepts.

control_tree_nodes.name: EVSE Capability
control_tree_nodes.definition: Current EVSE maximum voltage, current, and power boundaries; capability is not vehicle Request or actual output.

control_tree_nodes.name: Vehicle Capability
control_tree_nodes.definition: Current vehicle or battery allowed charging voltage, current, and power boundaries derived from battery, thermal, safety, and operating constraints.

control_tree_nodes.name: Vehicle Request
control_tree_nodes.definition: Vehicle charging voltage and current control targets; request power is normally derived as P_request = U_request × I_request unless independently defined and validated.

control_tree_nodes.name: Permission and Safety Gate
control_tree_nodes.definition: A decision result based on connection, lock, communication, parameters, battery conditions, HVIL, insulation, interface condition, and prohibiting faults; it is not contactor feedback or energy transfer.

control_tree_nodes.name: High-voltage path
control_tree_nodes.definition: High-voltage permission, contactor request, action, feedback, voltage matching, and confirmed DC path establishment are distinct steps requiring applicable evidence.

control_tree_nodes.name: Voltage and Current Actual
control_tree_nodes.definition: EVSE output voltage/current and Pack-side voltage/current are actual-response measurements at different boundaries; derived powers use synchronized voltage and current at the same boundary.

control_tree_nodes.name: Continuous charge control
control_tree_nodes.definition: Battery state and constraints update Vehicle Capability; EVSE Capability constrains feasible operation; Vehicle Request is updated; EVSE Actual and Pack Actual respond under system constraints. These roles remain distinct throughout charging.

control_tree_nodes.name: Thermal and protection control
control_tree_nodes.definition: Battery and interface temperature, cooling or heating demand and execution, HVIL, insulation, communication, voltage/current, lock, and fault conditions may update capability, limit request, or initiate protection without collapsing those roles.

control_tree_nodes.name: Stop and controlled exit
control_tree_nodes.definition: End condition, request reduction or withdrawal, actual-current reduction, energy-transfer exit, EVSE high-voltage exit, vehicle high-voltage-path exit, communication closeout, safe unlock, disconnect confirmation, and sleep preparation require bounded evidence; the initiator may remain unknown.
